{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to regression in global init logging and std::function overhead, and flagged conditional argument evaluation"
    },
    {
      "login": "purpleKarrot",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to singleton pattern usage in the logger and suggested a single-handler API"
    },
    {
      "login": "ryanofsky",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept and approach ACK, approved code review, suggested atomic callback count and MockTime API improvements"
    },
    {
      "login": "w0xlt",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "found potential resource leaks and deadlock risk on bad_alloc; later ACKed"
    },
    {
      "login": "musaHaruna",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "tested; raised concerns about cleanup callback execution order on allocation failure and behavior when user_data is null"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:2720705368",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher",
      "quote": "This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "changed approach to reviewer suggestion",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2721990582",
        "rc:2729164905",
        "c:3801642121"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2729164905",
      "status_by_quote": "I've changed the approach to your suggestion, so marking this as resolved."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2720709919",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection",
      "quote": "Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "indirection removed and PR no longer touches util/node logging",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2721327278",
        "rc:2736442108",
        "rc:3981133644"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "rc:2738597154"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3981133644",
      "status_by_quote": "The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3803203999",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Model the logging API after std::set_terminate without userdata and multiple connections since the logger is internally global",
      "quote": "I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that this concern is orthogonal to the PR",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:3804631039"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:3804631039",
      "status_by_quote": "I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had "
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3803203999",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Remove btck_logging_set_min_level since clients can apply their own filtering",
      "quote": "I also think that clients are able to apply their own filtering, so the btck_logging_set_min_level function can be removed.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author noted min level filtering avoids overhead of string formatting and argument evaluation for dropped logs",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:3804631039"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:3804631039",
      "status_by_quote": "They are, but I think it's reasonable to offer a (minimal) way for clients to avoid paying for overhead"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2730355874",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components",
      "quote": "Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author asked for alternative; ryanofsky noted the singleton can be removed later without API changes",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2731541954"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "rc:4100921691"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2731541954",
      "status_by_quote": "What do you suggest as an alternative?"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2734793117",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional",
      "quote": "I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "logging statements always evaluate arguments now",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:2736442108",
        "rc:2737382315",
        "c:3812232408"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2749146860",
      "status_by_quote": "The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate t"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3984322784",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration",
      "quote": "RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "fixed with RAII UserData and CallbackHandle wrappers",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3988186475",
        "rc:4006655804",
        "c:5679317242"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4006655804",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4030551866",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger",
      "quote": "If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "addressed deadlock scenario by constructing callback outside mutex",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4034240501",
        "c:5712024212"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5712024212",
      "status_by_quote": "Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100921884",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Add an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to avoid taking m_mutex and formatting strings when no callbacks are registered",
      "quote": "Minor: Log() takes m_mutex before checking m_callbacks.empty(), so when no logging connection is registered, every Info-and-above entry in every kernel thread still serializes on the mutex",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author re-added atomic callback count to KernelLogger to reduce lock acquisition",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106125573"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "r:5319606598",
      "status_by_quote": "added an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to reduce lock acquisition and unnecessary string formatting when no call"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100922070",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> instead of std::chrono::seconds for LogEntry::MockTime()",
      "quote": "Since LogEntry is new, it would seem more correct to return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> which is a time point not a duration",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author changed MockTime() to return optional sys_seconds",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106396988"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106396988",
      "status_by_quote": "Using sys_seconds now."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100922231",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Explain nanosecond precision and relation to other time values in the timestamp_ns doc comment",
      "quote": "Minor: since timestamp_ns is the only time value in the kernel API in nanoseconds... it might help to say both in the comment:",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author reworded docstring slightly and renamed mocktime to mocktime_s but kept comment concise",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106148902"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106148902",
      "status_by_quote": "I've only slightly reworded the docstring, there is nothing the user can/should do when their platform has a coarser time"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100922424",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Recommend against setting a minimum logging level above Info in the documentation",
      "quote": "it might be good for the doc to steer away from doing this, e.g.: \"Warning and Error entries report problems that usually need attention, so setting a minimum level above Info is not recommended for most applications.\"",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined, stating it is self-evident and kernel log statements should not be required for correct operation",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106383323"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106383323",
      "status_by_quote": "Going to leave this as-is. I think it's self-evident enough that warning and error logs are interesting to look at"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100922508",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Clarify in doc that btck_logging_set_min_level is global and applies to all connections",
      "quote": "Minor: after this PR the only function left that changes a logging setting is btck_logging_set_min_level, so this could be more specific",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined, preferring to keep the connection docstring general",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106356245"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106356245",
      "status_by_quote": "Going to leave this as-is. The globalness of btck_logging_set_min_level is already described in its docstring"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4100922585",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Format timestamp with seconds and fractional microseconds in bitcoin-chainstate output",
      "quote": "Not important: this prints the raw nanosecond count as the timestamp (e.g. 1758718542123456789). Maybe print seconds with a fractional part so it's readable at a glance",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined, preferring to wait for std::format support",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106417812"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106417812",
      "status_by_quote": "Going to leave this as-is. It seems (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36042) like we're reasonably close to being able to use std::format"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4101296912",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Intermediate commit causes assertion failure on btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) when compiled without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION",
      "quote": "calling btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) in a normal build hits the assert(false) until get_bclog_flag is removed in the last commit.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed the intermediate commit to avoid assertion failure without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4106493259"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4106493259",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4107768853",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Supplied cleanup callback is not called for non-null user_data if GetKernelLogger() throws during connection creation before main()",
      "quote": "The issue is that GetKernelLogger() is evaluated before the UserData argument is constructed. If it throws, the data has not yet been placed in the wrapper that would clean it up.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained GetKernelLogger() only returns a static reference so allocation cannot fail there",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4108928581"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4108928581",
      "status_by_quote": "GetKernelLogger() just returns a reference to a static variable, so I think this is fine either way"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4107770420",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Is skipping user_data_destroy_callback when user_data is null intended, and should the documentation clarify this requirement?",
      "quote": "Is skipping the cleanup callback when user_data is null intended?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author confirmed skipping is intended because there is nothing to free when user_data is null, and planned to assert and document it",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4108985828"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4108985828",
      "status_by_quote": "A null user_data and non-null user_data_destroy_callback is nonsensical and clearly a programmer error, so I think the correct approach is to assert this"
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:3813719678",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp",
        "src/logging.cpp",
        "src/util/log.h"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5310338619",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3719123369",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Dropping util::log::Dispatcher and implementing the log hooks directly in KernelLogger is simpler than routing through a dispatcher that only ever has one implementation per binary, and struct-based entries plus level-only filtering are a good simplification of the API.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp",
        "src/kernel/bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h",
        "src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h",
        "src/bitcoin-chainstate.cpp"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "promised assertion and documentation update for null user_data with non-null destroy callback",
      "id": "rc:4108985828"
    },
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "musaHaruna to acknowledge replies regarding GetKernelLogger construction order and null user_data handling",
      "id": "rc:4108928581"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Re-checked claims under the latest schema. Converted purpleKarrot's multi-connection critique into suggestions and added part 2 for dropping min-level filtering. Added ryanofsky's minor documentation and formatting suggestions, all of which were answered."
}

participants.note: objected to regression in global init logging and std::function overhead, and flagged conditional argument evaluation
objected to singleton pattern usage in the logger and suggested a single-handler API
Concept and approach ACK, approved code review, suggested atomic callback count and MockTime API improvements
found potential resource leaks and deadlock risk on bad_alloc; later ACKed
tested; raised concerns about cleanup callback execution order on allocation failure and behavior when user_data is null

claims.text: LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher
claims.quote: This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()
claims.status_by_quote: I've changed the approach to your suggestion, so marking this as resolved.

claims.text: Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection
claims.quote: Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.
claims.status_note: indirection removed and PR no longer touches util/node logging
claims.status_by_quote: The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all

claims.text: Model the logging API after std::set_terminate without userdata and multiple connections since the logger is internally global
claims.quote: I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well
claims.status_note: author replied that this concern is orthogonal to the PR
claims.status_by_quote: I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had

claims.text: Remove btck_logging_set_min_level since clients can apply their own filtering
claims.quote: I also think that clients are able to apply their own filtering, so the btck_logging_set_min_level function can be removed.
claims.status_note: author noted min level filtering avoids overhead of string formatting and argument evaluation for dropped logs
claims.status_by_quote: They are, but I think it's reasonable to offer a (minimal) way for clients to avoid paying for overhead

claims.text: Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components
claims.quote: Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.
claims.status_note: author asked for alternative; ryanofsky noted the singleton can be removed later without API changes
claims.status_by_quote: What do you suggest as an alternative?

claims.text: Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional
claims.quote: I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments
claims.status_note: logging statements always evaluate arguments now
claims.status_by_quote: The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate t

claims.text: Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration
claims.quote: RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.
claims.status_note: fixed with RAII UserData and CallbackHandle wrappers
claims.status_by_quote: Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper.

claims.text: Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger
claims.quote: If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.
claims.status_note: addressed deadlock scenario by constructing callback outside mutex
claims.status_by_quote: Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt

claims.text: Add an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to avoid taking m_mutex and formatting strings when no callbacks are registered
claims.quote: Minor: Log() takes m_mutex before checking m_callbacks.empty(), so when no logging connection is registered, every Info-and-above entry in every kernel thread still serializes on the mutex
claims.status_note: author re-added atomic callback count to KernelLogger to reduce lock acquisition
claims.status_by_quote: added an atomic callback count to KernelLogger to reduce lock acquisition and unnecessary string formatting when no call

claims.text: Return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> instead of std::chrono::seconds for LogEntry::MockTime()
claims.quote: Since LogEntry is new, it would seem more correct to return std::optional<std::chrono::sys_seconds> which is a time point not a duration
claims.status_note: author changed MockTime() to return optional sys_seconds

claims.text: Explain nanosecond precision and relation to other time values in the timestamp_ns doc comment
claims.quote: Minor: since timestamp_ns is the only time value in the kernel API in nanoseconds... it might help to say both in the comment:
claims.status_note: author reworded docstring slightly and renamed mocktime to mocktime_s but kept comment concise
claims.status_by_quote: I've only slightly reworded the docstring, there is nothing the user can/should do when their platform has a coarser time

claims.text: Recommend against setting a minimum logging level above Info in the documentation
claims.quote: it might be good for the doc to steer away from doing this, e.g.: "Warning and Error entries report problems that usually need attention, so setting a minimum level above Info is not recommended for most applications."
claims.status_note: author declined, stating it is self-evident and kernel log statements should not be required for correct operation
claims.status_by_quote: Going to leave this as-is. I think it's self-evident enough that warning and error logs are interesting to look at

claims.text: Clarify in doc that btck_logging_set_min_level is global and applies to all connections
claims.quote: Minor: after this PR the only function left that changes a logging setting is btck_logging_set_min_level, so this could be more specific
claims.status_note: author declined, preferring to keep the connection docstring general
claims.status_by_quote: Going to leave this as-is. The globalness of btck_logging_set_min_level is already described in its docstring

claims.text: Format timestamp with seconds and fractional microseconds in bitcoin-chainstate output
claims.quote: Not important: this prints the raw nanosecond count as the timestamp (e.g. 1758718542123456789). Maybe print seconds with a fractional part so it's readable at a glance
claims.status_note: author declined, preferring to wait for std::format support
claims.status_by_quote: Going to leave this as-is. It seems (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36042) like we're reasonably close to being able to use std::format

claims.text: Intermediate commit causes assertion failure on btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) when compiled without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION
claims.quote: calling btck_logging_enable_category(btck_LogCategory_LOCK) in a normal build hits the assert(false) until get_bclog_flag is removed in the last commit.
claims.status_note: author fixed the intermediate commit to avoid assertion failure without DEBUG_LOCKCONTENTION

claims.text: Supplied cleanup callback is not called for non-null user_data if GetKernelLogger() throws during connection creation before main()
claims.quote: The issue is that GetKernelLogger() is evaluated before the UserData argument is constructed. If it throws, the data has not yet been placed in the wrapper that would clean it up.
claims.status_note: author explained GetKernelLogger() only returns a static reference so allocation cannot fail there
claims.status_by_quote: GetKernelLogger() just returns a reference to a static variable, so I think this is fine either way

claims.text: Is skipping user_data_destroy_callback when user_data is null intended, and should the documentation clarify this requirement?
claims.quote: Is skipping the cleanup callback when user_data is null intended?
claims.status_note: author confirmed skipping is intended because there is nothing to free when user_data is null, and planned to assert and document it
claims.status_by_quote: A null user_data and non-null user_data_destroy_callback is nonsensical and clearly a programmer error, so I think the correct approach is to assert this

support.reason: Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API

Dropping util::log::Dispatcher and implementing the log hooks directly in KernelLogger is simpler than routing through a dispatcher that only ever has one implementation per binary, and struct-based entries plus level-only filtering are a good simplification of the API.
